chunks: Amir al-Mu'mineen (peace be upon him) sent Abdullah ibn al-Abbas to Ibn al-Kawwa' and his companions, and upon him (Ibn al-Abbas) was a thin shirt and a garment. When they looked at him, they said: 'O Ibn Abbas! You are the best among us in our own eyes, yet you wear such clothing?' He replied: 'And this is the first matter I dispute with you:'
[7:32] Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He has brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?
And He said: [7:31] Take to your adornments at every mosque.

key_terms.أخاصمكم: I dispute/argue with you — used in the context of religious debate and argumentation from scripture
key_terms.ابن الكواء: Ibn al-Kawwa' — a Kharijite leader known for his encounters with Imam Ali
key_terms.الطيبات من الرزق: The good provisions — wholesome and permissible sustenance
key_terms.حلة: A full garment/set of fine clothing, typically a matching upper and lower garment
key_terms.زينة الله: The adornments of God — created blessings including clothing and fine things

ai.seo_question: Is wearing fine clothing permissible in Islam according to the Quran and Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) sent Abdullah ibn Abbas as an emissary to the Kharijite leader Ibn al-Kawwa' and his group. When they criticized Ibn Abbas for wearing fine clothing, he responded by citing two Quranic verses (7:32 and 7:31) affirming that God's adornments and good provisions are not forbidden. This hadith establishes the permissibility of wearing good clothing and refutes the Kharijite tendency toward excessive asceticism, situating the debate in the historical context of early Islamic divisions over piety and outward religious practice.
